newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAFRICA'S EQUITY OPTIONS MARKET MAY BE PUT ON HOLD.
newsitem.headline: SAFRICA'S EQUITY OPTIONS MARKET MAY BE PUT ON HOLD.

text.p: South Africa's planned Equity Options Market (EOM) may be put on hold after failing to attract applications for the full 75 seats on offer, Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) executive president Russell Loubser said on Wednesday.
EOM, planned for launch in October, would list standardised American style scrip-settled call and put options on the equities underlying the ALSI40, GLDI10, INDI25 and FINDI30 indices.
But firm offers had been received for only 50 of the seats by last Friday's deadline, although eight more were likely to be taken up.
Loubser told a news conference on the release of the JSE's 1996 annual report that at least 70 seats would have to be taken up before the project could go ahead.
"Either the market wants it or we leave it for another day...if we get 70 I am happy to make a decision either way, 70 is close to 75," he said.
The final allocation date for the seats is March 28 and Loubser said financial insitutions were being chased to see if they wanted the seats.
He said the cautious market reaction was typical of an emerging market financial centre. "People play a wait and see attitude," he said.
The seats cost 85,000 rand each and are priced to cover the start-up costs of the market. If less than 75 seats are sold the JSE will post a loss on the project.
But Loubser said not all the start-up costs came at once and that if the market did get going with less than the required number to break even it could attract other players later.
"It is not closed forever. People may come in when they see things are working," he said.
If it goes ahead, trading on EOM will be initially conducted on a screen and telephone basis before moving to an automated system at a later date.
